title: 26. Kirkham

body: Top lips. This question was on deferred tax. Part (a) might have confused you — the requirement to state how the
tax base Is computed could be read as asking for a discussion of tax rules. Tax rules vary as to the specific tax
jurisdiction and this is outside the scope of a DipIFR exam. What was actually being asked for is an explanation of
some definitions from IAS 12 — the ACCA's answer follows the text of IAS 12 very closely. This was a difficult
requirement, and it was important that you did not exceed your time limit when trying to answer it.
Part (b) should have been a bit easier, It is important that your answers here are as specific as possible, for
example in Exhibit 1 stating that the deferred tax liability would be non-current. It is also important that you do not
overlook the mention in the requirement of current tax, and that your answers make use of the official terminology
Easy marks, This was a difficult question, Dut the easy marks are for the calculations, which should have been
within reach. The easiest of these is in calculating the final deferred tax asset or liability. using the tax rate of 25%.

{a} The tax base of an asset is the amount which will be deductible for tax purposes against any taxable
economic benefits which will flow to the entity when the asset is recovered. If these benefits are not
taxable, the tax base equals the carrying amount.
The tax base of a liability is its carrying amount, less any amount which will be deductible for tax purposes
in respect of that liability in future periods. If the ‘liability’ is revenue received in advance, the tax base is its
carrying amount, less any revenue which will not be taxable in future periods.
